FILE: ./clip_words_check.py — prove a rendered clip contains the material it was selected from.

CLI: clip_words_check.py --manifest PATH --stems DIR [--clips-dir DIR] [--json OUT]

The manifest is a polished_clips_manifest.json (read one under /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/*/clips/ for the real shape: entries carry raw_start_s/raw_end_s, final_start_s/final_end_s, and per-variant output files). For each clip entry: extract the clip file's audio, extract the SOURCE window from the correct speaker stem at raw_start_s..raw_end_s (determine the speaker by which stem carries more energy in that window), cross-correlate, and require the clip's audio to LOCATE inside the source window (peak and margin thresholds like the certifier's) at a lag consistent with the manifest's mapping. A clip whose audio does not locate in its claimed source span is cut from the wrong place; report the actual best-match lag so the operator can see how far off it is. Exit 1 if ANY clip fails; list every clip with per-clip verdicts either way.

FILE: ./cut_absence_check.py — prove removed spans are actually absent from the rendered program, from the media itself.

CLI: cut_absence_check.py --render PATH --stems DIR --cuts JSON [--json OUT]

--cuts is a JSON file: a list of {"id": str, "start_s": float, "end_s": float} in SESSION-GRID seconds (the caller exports these from the applied edit plan). For each cut: extract that span's audio from the loudest-speaker stem (skip spans where both stems are silent, reporting them as UNMEASURABLE, not passed); cross-correlate against the FULL rendered program's audio; the span must NOT locate anywhere (peak below the locate threshold, or located only with a weak margin). A confidently-located cut span means the cut was not applied. ALSO verify the inverse control on each run: pick two KEPT windows adjacent to cuts and require them to LOCATE — a run whose controls fail cannot certify anything and exits 2. Exit 1 if any cut span is found in the render.

FILE: ./speaker_attribution_check.py — prove the camera shown is the person speaking.

CLI: speaker_attribution_check.py --render PATH --boundaries PATH --stems DIR --offsets JSON [--tolerance FLOAT] [--json OUT]

--boundaries is the render's .boundaries.json sidecar (find one under /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/*/processed/ and read it for the real shape: segments with source-session spans, the chosen angle per segment, and edited-time offsets). --offsets maps angle labels to speaker stems, e.g. {"host": "host_audio.flac", "guest": "guest_audio.flac"}. For each segment longer than a minimum (short reaction shots are legitimate style; default the minimum to 4.0s and say why): measure mean RMS dBFS of each speaker's stem over the segment's SOURCE span; if one speaker dominates by a margin (named constant, suggest 6 dB with rationale) and the segment's angle shows the OTHER speaker, that segment fails. Segments inside a known camera-dropout forced-switch window are exempt if the caller passes --dropout-holes JSON (list of {at_abs_s, duration_s}); read the exemption from that file rather than guessing. Report per-segment: span, angle shown, host dBFS, guest dBFS, verdict. Exit 1 on any failure.

FILE: ./bumper_check.py — prove bumpers are present, at the right ends, exactly once, and level-matched.

CLI: bumper_check.py --final PATH --intro PATH --outro PATH [--tolerance-lu FLOAT] [--json OUT]

PRESENCE: cross-correlate the intro bumper's audio against the FIRST (intro duration + 10s) of the final render — it must locate at approximately lag 0. Same for the outro against the LAST window, locating so it ENDS at approximately the file end. UNIQUENESS: correlate each bumper against the full program body between the bumpers; a confident match there means a bumper leaked into the middle — fail. LEVELS: measure integrated loudness (EBU R128 via ffmpeg loudnorm print_format=json or ebur128 filter — state which and why) for the intro span, the outro span, and the program body; the bumper-to-body delta must be within --tolerance-lu (default 3.0 LU, named constant with rationale). Report all three loudness numbers and both locate lags. Exit 1 on missing, duplicated, misplaced, or level-mismatched bumpers.
